clue.text: Shepherdess and worker keeping operation quiet

indicators.note: the worker holds the operation within itself, as if keeping it safe

parts.note: a bee is the classic crossword worker
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A shepherdess and a farmhand keep a medical operation hushed up.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Bo-Peep is the nursery-rhyme shepherdess who lost her sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme character is famous precisely as a girl tending a flock.

clue.text: Very important programme led initially by European in US city

parts.note: big means important, as in a big decision
an app is a computer program

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word led

explanation.surface: An important show, fronted by a European, takes place in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Apple is the familiar nickname for New York City.

clue.text: Before start of gala French city displays state of expectation

parts.note: pre is the prefix meaning before

indicators.note: start of takes the first letter of the gala word

parts.note: Nancy is a city in north-eastern France

explanation.surface: Ahead of a gala, a French city is full of anticipation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State of expectation' sounds like mere anticipation, but an expectant mother is carrying a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: Expecting is the idiom for carrying a child, so the condition of a mother-to-be fits.

clue.text: Stops endlessly providing comfort

indicators.note: endlessly means the stops word loses both its end letters

parts.note: ceases means stops

explanation.surface: Something that never stops brings comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease means freedom from pain or worry, a state of comfort; both also work as verbs.

clue.text: Dance with German in grass is shaken up

indicators.note: the dance and German sit inside the grass word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet ground
a jig is a lively folk dance

explanation.surface: Someone dances with a German in the long grass and comes away shaken.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejig is to rearrange or reorganise, so something rejigged has been reshuffled.

clue.text: Beryl starts to enjoy my entertaining repartee at Lady's Day

indicators.note: the starts of the seven words that follow are their first letters

explanation.surface: A woman called Beryl begins to enjoy the witty banter at a ladies' race day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beryl' looks like a woman's name, but it is the mineral. Ladies' Day is a fashionable day at a race meeting such as Royal Ascot.
explanation.definitionFit: The green gemstone is a variety of the mineral beryl coloured by chromium.

clue.text: I stupefied manic sons — they can't fall asleep

indicators.note: stupefied means dazed and muddled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A parent drugs their hyperactive sons, who still won't drop off.
explanation.definitionFit: People with chronic sleeplessness are unable to drop off at night.

clue.text: Jar reported to be large

indicators.note: reported means the word is heard as spoken rather than written

parts.note: to grate is to jar, as a harsh noise jars on the nerves

explanation.surface: A pot is said to be big.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jar' looks like a container noun; it is the verb meaning to irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: Great and large are synonyms for big in size.

clue.text: Religious scholar taking part in benefit picnic

indicators.note: the scholar joins in by going inside the benefit word

parts.note: the dole is British unemployment benefit
DD is Doctor of Divinity

explanation.surface: A theologian joins a charity picnic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picnic' looks like an outdoor meal; it is informal for an easy task.
explanation.definitionFit: No picnic means hard going, so a picnic is a very easy task; doddle is British slang for the same.

clue.text: Bird to start to undo container

indicators.note: the start of the undo word is its first letter

parts.note: a can is a container

explanation.surface: A bird begins to open a container.
explanation.definitionFit: The toucan is a tropical American bird with a huge colourful beak.

clue.text: Erupting geyser not producing volcanic material

indicators.note: an eruption blasts things apart, so the letters of the following words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A geyser bursts up but brings no lava or rock with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Greystone is a grey volcanic rock, a compact basalt-like lava.

clue.text: Hack putting time into source

indicators.note: the time letter is put into the middle of the source word

parts.note: a seed is the source from which something grows

explanation.surface: A hack journalist inserts the time into a story's source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' suggests a journalist, but here it is an old riding horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A hack is an ordinary riding horse, and a steed is a literary word for a horse.

clue.text: Champagne socialist possibly having short drink with king

indicators.note: short means the drink word loses its final letter

parts.note: a pint is a drink of beer
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A wealthy left-winger has a quick drink with a king.
explanation.walkthrough: Pink describes someone mildly left-wing; a champagne socialist is a well-off person with such views.
explanation.definitionFit: Pink is used of politics that are leftish but not fully red, fitting a comfortable socialist.

clue.text: Fight encountered by a liberal recycling material

parts.note: a scrap is a scuffle or fight
met is the past tense of meet, to encounter

explanation.surface: A brawl breaks out between someone and a Liberal over recycling.
explanation.definitionFit: Discarded metal is collected and melted down for reuse, so it is material for recycling.

clue.text: Sketch skin art popular around old estate

parts.note: a plan is a sketch or drawing
tat is short for tattoo

indicators.note: the popular word goes around the old letter

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: Someone designs popular tattoos showing an old country estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A plantation is a large farm estate growing crops such as cotton or tea.

clue.text: Fat from sheep placed across tips of noisettes of lamb

indicators.note: the placed word is laid across the tips, so they end up inside it

parts.note: lain is the past participle of lie, so placed or set down

indicators.note: the tips of the three words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Sheep fat has been spread over the ends of some lamb noisettes.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanolin is the greasy wax taken from sheep's wool, used in skin creams.

clue.text: Doctor one pages with second of symptoms is pathetic

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: second of picks the second letter of the symptoms word

explanation.surface: A doctor pages someone about a second set of symptoms and seems feeble.
explanation.definitionFit: Drippy is informal for weak, wet and ineffectual, much the same as pathetic.

clue.text: Appropriate to live by a church somewhere in Florida

parts.note: to palm is to take or steal, so appropriate
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: A person takes over a home beside a church somewhere in Florida.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb meaning to take.
explanation.definitionFit: Palm Beach is a wealthy resort town on Florida's Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Plant the French sell to queen

parts.note: la is French for the, feminine form
to vend is to sell
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: French people sell a plant to the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavender is a fragrant shrub with purple flower spikes.

clue.text: Young bird sounds like small seal

indicators.note: the clue says outright that the answer is said like another word

parts.note: a signet is a small seal, as on a signet ring

explanation.surface: A baby bird is said to resemble a little seal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seal' tempts as the animal, but it is the stamp for wax.
explanation.definitionFit: A cygnet is a young swan, a juvenile bird.

clue.text: Article covering broken limb that provides protection from pins and needles

definitions.text: that provides protection from pins and needles

indicators.note: the article wraps around the jumbled limb letters

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: broken means the limb letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A medical item covering a broken limb guards against tingling pins and needles.
explanation.walkthrough: Pins and needles reads as the tingling of a numb limb, but here means real sewing pins.
explanation.definitionFit: A sewing cap worn on the fingertip shields it from being pricked while stitching.

clue.text: Heartless trainer on field finds part of ear

indicators.note: heartless means the trainer word loses its central letter

parts.note: a coach is a sports trainer
lea is a poetic word for a meadow or field

explanation.surface: An uncaring coach out on the pitch discovers something about the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: The cochlea is the spiral cavity of the inner ear that turns sound into nerve signals.

clue.text: Material in bed not turned over

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: turned over means the word not is flipped back to front

explanation.surface: Fabric in a bed that hasn't been turned.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotton is a fabric woven from the fibre of the cotton plant.

clue.text: Part of magic act uses plant

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A magician's routine makes use of a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The cactus is a spiny succulent plant of dry regions.

clue.text: Echo in song registers for high flying performers

indicators.note: the echo letter is placed inside the song word

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera
Echo is E in the NATO phonetic alphabet
lists are registers or rolls of names

explanation.surface: An echo in a song registers for performers who soar high.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerialists are acrobats on trapezes or high wires, performing far above the ground.

clue.text: Artist breaking law taking drug in countryside

indicators.note: taking here means removing the drug letter
the artist breaks into the middle of the law word

parts.note: a rule is a law
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
E is ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: An artist breaks the law by taking drugs out in the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' puts RA into RULE to give RURALE, and 'taking' takes away the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural describes things belonging to or found out in the country rather than the town.

clue.text: Competent leader removed from board

indicators.note: the first letter, the leader, comes off the board word

parts.note: a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A capable chairman is ousted from the board.
explanation.definitionFit: Able and competent are synonyms meaning having the skill to do something.

clue.text: Dress old lady by one

parts.note: ma is a mother, an old lady in slang
X is the times sign, as in four by two
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A mother stands beside someone in a frock.
explanation.definitionFit: A maxi is a long dress or skirt reaching the ankles.

clue.text: Is traitor returning bones?

indicators.note: returning means the two words together are read backwards

parts.note: a rat is a betrayer or traitor

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a traitor is coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns IS RAT back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarsi are the bones of the ankle, plural of tarsus.

clue.text: Abhor aid distributed to contain unknown source of disease potentially

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap around the unknown
distributed means the letters are spread about and rearranged

parts.note: Z is an algebraic unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: Aid workers hate handing out supplies that hold an unknown infection risk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distributed' suggests handing out aid, but it signals the rearrangement; 'potentially' makes the definition fair, since a hazard is a possible source.
explanation.definitionFit: A biohazard is a biological risk to health, such as infectious material that might spread illness.

clue.text: Special place to bury Chip

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
to inter is to bury

explanation.surface: A special place is set aside for burying a chip.
explanation.definitionFit: A splinter is a small sharp fragment broken off, just like a chip of wood.

clue.text: Woman in tree is angler

indicators.note: the woman word is set inside the tree word

parts.note: a fir is a coniferous tree
she is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman perched up a tree turns out to be fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: A fisher is someone who fishes, and an angler fishes with rod and line.
